issue: The caption makes a countable claim the figure cannot support: 'the faint vertical rules inside the KV budget show those 24.9 GB request slots'. Two problems. (a) Legibility: the orange KV region is filled with a regular white dot hatch, and the 'faint vertical rules' are not visually separable from that hatch at print size, so a reader cannot distinguish slot boundaries from fill texture. (b) Counting: 436/24.9 = 17.51 slots is not an integer, so the bar must contain 17 full slots plus a half slot; if the rules are drawn at slot boundaries there will be 18 rules, and counting them yields 18 — the exact wrong answer the caption spends a clause pre-empting ('floor 17, not 18'). The figure thus risks teaching the error it warns against.
evidence: 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB/request = 17.51. The caption's own text: 'C ≈ 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18; the faint vertical rules inside the KV budget show those 24.9 GB request slots)'. Rendered page: the orange region shows a uniform dot texture; no distinct slot boundaries are resolvable at 150 dpi.
acceptance_test: Make the slot boundaries a distinct, higher-contrast element (e.g. white gaps or a solid 1-pt rule) that is clearly different from the fill hatch, and draw exactly 17 full slots plus one visibly half-width slot, with a small '17 + ½' annotation. If the rules cannot be made countable, delete the parenthetical claim about the rules and keep the arithmetic in the caption only.

issue: The figure asserts 'in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request' and then '→ ~17 requests' with no statement of the operating assumption. The identity only holds if every in-flight request holds the full canonical KV (i.e. every request has run to completion-length context). In a live server, requests at different stages hold different amounts of KV, so 17.5 is a worst-case ceiling on simultaneously-full-length requests, not an expected concurrency. The caption's phrase 'max-FP16 KV' reads as 'maximum precision FP16' and does not carry the worst-case assumption, so a reader can easily take 17.5 as the average concurrency the host will sustain.
evidence: Figure text: 'in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request' and '≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'. Caption: 'at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C ≈ 17.5 concurrent'. No statement anywhere on the page that each in-flight request is assumed to hold the full 9.5K/9.2K-token KV.
acceptance_test: Add the assumption to the figure itself, e.g. 'in-flight (all at full context) = KV budget ÷ KV per request', and add one clause to the caption: 'this is a worst-case ceiling: it assumes every in-flight request holds the full canonical KV; average concurrency will be higher for shorter requests.' Cross-check that the same assumption is stated wherever 17.5 is reused later in the book.

evidence: Rendered page: the line above the equation shows a clear '÷' in 'KV budget ÷ KV per request'; the operator in the equation below does not show the two dots of a '÷' at the same resolution and reads as '+'. page: PDF 148 / printed 128; PDF 149 / printed 129; PDF 162 / printed 142
figure: FIGURE 7.7 (Concurrency budget), FIGURE 7.8 (Memory Tetris), FIGURE 8.2 (roofline prefill point)
issue: Three figures in two chapters use two different canonical context lengths, and the difference changes a load-bearing, explicitly-defended number. FIG 7.7's caption derives concurrency from '24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV' and concludes 'C ≈ 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18)'; FIG 7.8's first tier is labelled '9.5K context = 229 GB used'. But 24.9 GB corresponds to 9,500 tokens at the book's canonical 2.62 MB/token FP16 KV, whereas FIG 8.2 uses '9.2K' as the canonical prefill length. At 9.2K tokens the per-request FP16 KV is 9,200 × 2.62144 MB = 24.12 GB, and 436 GB ÷ 24.12 GB = 18.08 → 18 concurrent — the exact value the FIG 7.7 caption pre-empts ('floor 17, not 18'). The reader cannot reconcile 9.5K with 9.2K from the figures, and the 'not 18' parenthetical is only true under the 9.5K reading.
evidence: Recomputed: 2 (K,V) × 80 layers × 64 heads × 128 dim × 2 B = 2.62144 MB/token (book's canonical 2.62). 9,500 × 2.62144 MB = 24.90 GB → 436/24.90 = 17.51 → 17. 9,200 × 2.62144 MB = 24.12 GB → 436/24.12 = 18.08 → 18. FIG 7.8's own arithmetic confirms the 9.5K basis: 24.9 + 140 + 64 = 229 GB (printed), 84 + 140 + 64 = 288 GB (printed), 335 + 140 + 64 = 539 GB (printed). The book's canonical request is 1,200 + 8,000 = 9,200 tokens, so the 9.5K tier is unexplained by anything visible on these pages.
acceptance_test: State one canonical context length for the memory chapter and use it in both figures. If the canonical is 9,200 tokens: change FIG 7.7's '24.9 GB/request' to 24.1 GB, change the concurrency to '≈ 18.1 → 18', change the FP8 figure to 12.06 GB/request and '≈36', and change FIG 7.8's first tier from '9.5K context = 229 GB used' to '9.2K context = 228 GB used' (24.1 + 140 + 64). If 9.5K is deliberate, add one sentence in Ch 7 defining the 9.5K canonical request and its relation to the 9,200-token workload used elsewhere, and add the token count to FIG 7.7's caption. Either way, the 'floor 17, not 18' parenthetical must be re-derived from the number actually printed.

issue: The caption's parenthetical '(17.5 → 11 at 32K; 436/335 = 1.30 → 1 at 128K)' appears to print '11' as the concurrency at 32K context. issue: The figure's closing note reads 'not every component shown — the gradient makes compute, memory, bandwidth, capacity and interconnect distance constraints'.
